title: Shopping Cart with a class and Aggregate Initialization
prompt_md:
## Goal
Introduce the `class` keyword. Define a class with public data members and let the driver create objects with aggregate initialization. Compute a shopping cart's line-item subtotals and grand total.

## Input
- Line 1: an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 100), the number of line items.
- Next N lines: two integers `price quantity` per line.

## Output
- For each line item, one line: `Subtotal: <price * quantity>`.
- After the last item, one line: `Total: <sum of all subtotals>`.

## What to build
Define a class `Item` with two public data members (`int price` and `int quantity`) and a free function `int subtotal(const Item& it)`. The driver creates each item with aggregate initialization (`Item it{ price, quantity };`), which only compiles if your members are public and declared in that order. Member functions arrive in the next lesson, so keep the behavior in the free function for now.

title: Durations: a class, Aggregate Init, and a Free Function
prompt_md:
## Goal
Use a `class` with public data members and aggregate initialization to model durations. Report each duration in minutes, then the grand total formatted as hours and minutes.

## Input
- Line 1: an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 100), the number of durations.
- Next N lines: two integers `hours minutes` per line.

## Output
- For each duration, one line: `Minutes: <total minutes of that duration>`.
- After the last one, a final line: `Total: H:MM`, where H is the combined hours and MM is the leftover minutes, zero-padded to two digits.

## What to build
Define a class `Time` with public data members `int hours` and `int minutes`, and a free function `int toMinutes(const Time& t)`. The driver aggregate-initializes each `Time` and handles the `H:MM` formatting.
